title: Does Veronese remove the fixed-linear-space smoothness obstruction?
as_he_states: After observing that the dual discriminant may contain all hyperplanes through a positive-dimensional fixed linear space C, the author suggests this may become impossible for phi_n f with n≥2 and says the question could be posed in a remark (scan81,3283–3292).
plausible_today: The unrestricted answer is no, already for v₂(P²) and C=V(U_x²,U_y²)≅P³. A meaningful positive variant must impose first-jet conditions along the base; smoothness off it is a different assertion.
state_of_art: As of19November2026. Wutz2016 Theorem1.2 gives the finite-field sufficient conditions V_m=empty and dim(V_e)+e<m for e<m, where m=dim X and V_e is the embedding-dimension stratum of the prescribed base. This is asymptotic in degree. The unrestricted question has a negative answer by the explicit pencil a x²+b y² constructed here. Stacks33.47.1 and33.47.3 distinguish smoothness away from a fixed base subscheme from the first-jet obstruction at its points. Wutz2016 Theorem1.2 gives a finite-field analogue with embedding-dimension restrictions, not an unrestricted fixed-linear-space theorem. No historical priority is claimed for this counterexample.
why_open: The suggestion is explicitly tentative. No reason for its absence from a later treatment is supplied.
worth: The unrestricted hope is closed by an elementary counterexample; further work is useful only to formulate and compare the missing base-jet hypotheses.

title: The promised general divisor functor
as_he_states: Inside the cancelled scan112 paragraph, the author promises to prove in ChapterV that Div_(X/S) is representable for projective X/S; the preceding hypotheses are flatness and local finite presentation.
plausible_today: For a projective flat finitely presented morphism, relative effective Cartier divisors form an open subfunctor of the Hilbert functor. Keep this distinct from a fixed-L component and from P(E).
state_of_art: As of19November2026. Grothendieck’s Bourbaki232 Proposition4.1 (1962), printed152, is the exact projective-flat representability statement over a locally noetherian base: Div is an open subfunctor of Hilb. The arbitrary-base finite-presentation version uses noetherian approximation in addition. The deleted manuscript promise has no independently established date relative to this publication; classA records its own-publication counterpart without a claim of historical priority.
why_open: The promised treatment is not given in this cancelled passage; its cancellation does not supply a reason for abandonment.
worth: No new representability theorem is needed; a precise concordance to the1962 proposition and its noetherian hypotheses completes the useful task.
